writ.stamp gained a clause this round — 'Past it, no one tells you a thing you have not asked for. So ask them what they do, and what is being said here.' It is diegetic, well written and spoken by a character, and it is still the game explaining its central verb, on the one path this piece owns that says the world does not explain itself. status_reasons: Overall 1.3 (mean of RI-JRN09 2, RI-JRN01 2, RI-EXP01 0) against a wave-1 gate of 7.0. The min over the three gates is 0; mean is reported as the headline only so the number stays comparable with round 1's 1.3, and both readings are FAIL.

IT IS THE SAME 1.3 AS ROUND 1 AND IT DOES NOT MEAN THE SAME THING. RI-JRN09 went from native 55 to 92 and RI-JRN01 from 0.582 to 0.772 of runnable. Three caps moved onto three new defects; two of the three are one-line repairs.

BLOCKING: creation cannot be completed by a player. Engine._titleApply('new') calls censusBegin({}) with no race; Census.observe() is the only setter and nothing on the play path calls it; the census throws at writ.race-observed, the throw is caught, and the player reads 'race must be observed before the scene reaches the desk' in the dialogue panel with no way forward.

BLOCKING: the name a player types is not the name recorded. input/real.js consults the move map and the control map before onTextChar, so 14 of 26 letters, digits 1-4 and Space never reach the text field, and KeyE (interact) COMMITS the node mid-word. Predicted character-for-character from game/data/input/profiles.json and confirmed live: 'Silt-Under-Salt' -> 'il-Un'.

BLOCKING (RI-JRN09 HF1): DTR 0.000 at hold.out. Jeeh-Ei's own line is never drawn anywhere and her reply to the name the player just typed is drawn one node later in the Writ House above a different speaker.
HF5 (RI-JRN01 M13): the journey completes on 0 of 4 input modalities, and separately the build's recorded O17 4/4 is two button presses on the title surface, not the journey the check describes.

RI-EXP01 unmeasurable => 0, fail-closed. Hard fails 2, 3 and 4 are literally satisfied by the numbers and are deliberately NOT fired: firing them makes the whole wave DEAD under PLAYTHROUGH-CRITIC §2 on an artifact of who ran the session. Round 1 declined for the same reason and was right.

CREDIT, measured not assumed: round 1's single biggest gap is CLOSED (the register now sees the vector glyph path; M9 searches 4 real strings instead of 0); HF3 is closed; the touch leg is closed; and O6 — the item's own How-we-lose #5 and the whole Morrowind comparison — is repaired and measures 61.5 s against a 60 s bar.

biggest_gap.what: Engine._titleApply('new') — the row the title's `New` commits to — calls censusBegin({}) with no options. Census.spec.race is set by exactly one function, Census.observe(race), called from exactly one place: censusBegin, when opts.race is present. So on the player's path race is never observed, and Census.answer() at writ.race-observed throws 'race must be observed before the scene reaches the desk'. _censusApplyPending() catches it, emits census_refused and draws the reason on the surface, so the player is left in front of the Warden-Scribe reading an engine error string as dialogue, with no way forward and no way out of the room (the Writ House door is held until you are written down).
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: Every number this piece has ever published — DTR 0.982, AC 6 of 7, NAMED 14 of 14, the writ carried out, 61.5 s of body before the first question — was taken on a scene that only the harness can open, because the harness supplies the one creation input the player never gives. NEXT-DISPATCH §P calls this piece the binding gate for handing the owner a playable build; a person who clones this repo, serves it and presses New cannot make a character or reach the world. The corpus's own driver reproduces the defect and cannot see it: journey-run.mjs opens with censusBegin({}) too and walks the scene inside `catch { break; }`, so it reports M4 clause 1 as 'N/A — no character-field-writing event in the trace' instead of as a failure.

remedy.action: Observe the race of the body the player is actually in at the moment `New` begins the scene. RI-CHR01 §1 row 2 is explicit that race is observed and never asked, so the value must come from the body — which means the choice of that body is W1-07's and must exist before this can be done honestly. A hardcoded default would satisfy the acceptance test below and betray the item, so the acceptance names that too. Separately, replace journey-run.mjs's bare `catch { break; }` at the census walk with a recorded failure, so the driver can never again report an absence as N/A.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/journey/census-newgame.mjs exits 0 with player_can_finish_creation true; AND node tools/journey/opening-play.mjs reaches P10 with the census past writ.race-observed, driven only through real DOM input from the title, with zero census_refused events in the run; AND the race the character ends up with is one the player chose or the body already had, not a constant in the source.

secondary_observations.what: GAP-W1-26-the-name-you-type-is-not-the-name-recorded (blocking, journey.opening.exchange). input/real.js handles keydown as move map, then control map, then text — so A C D E F G M R S T V W X Z, digits 1-4 and Space never reach the text field, and KeyE is `interact`, which commits the node mid-word. Two arms: 'Hio-Junnilo' (no bound characters) round-trips verbatim; 'Silt-Under-Salt' comes back 'il-Un' with an early commit. The prediction was made from the bindings data before the browser was opened and held character for character. Acceptance: node tools/journey/name-entry.mjs exits 0 with both arms verbatim, including a name containing E, S, A and a space.

GAP-W1-26-orphan-reply-at-the-hand-back-node (blocking, journey.opening.legibility). RI-JRN09 HF1. Acceptance: jrn09-exchange.mjs exits 0 with no HF1, DTR(hold.out) >= 0.90, and Jeeh-Ei's reply to the hatch-name drawn in the barge hold with her as the attributed speaker.

The HUD — a health bar, a stamina bar, a purse reading 5, the stance readout LIGHT and the equipped spell 'Spark-Da…' — is painted on the TITLE SCREEN at first launch, before any character exists, and stays up through the barge hold. Not a marker, so not HF4, but a first-launch title showing a stranger's health bar is a journey.firstlaunch.flow defect and this piece owns that path. Visible in docs/shots/2026-08-08-w1-26-r2-01-title-first-launch.png.
'Spark-Da…' — the equipped-spell field truncates its own content with an ellipsis on the HUD at 640x360. journey.opening.legibility.

M10: the opening ships zero in-world inscriptions, and the barge hold already has a prop named `tally_scratch`. The DS/OPEN #4 mechanism has its fiction authored and nothing attached to it — the cheapest 4 points in RI-JRN01.

There is no README.md at the repo root and no start/serve script in package.json, so NEXT-DISPATCH §P gate item 1's 'one command' does not exist. A person must know to serve the tree over http:// themselves; file:// cannot work, because the entry is an ES module and game/data is fetched.

Play mode delivered 1.52 sim fps at the title and 2.91 in world at 640x360 under loadavg 19.9-25.6 on four cores with three to four other agents' browsers resident. Reported as a CONDITION on every number in this verdict and explicitly NOT as a claim about the build's frame rate on a machine with a GPU. It is why O6's 60 s was taken on the piece's own probe rather than in my real-input run.

method_deviations.deviation: I wrote three instruments of my own — tools/journey/opening-play.mjs, census-newgame.mjs and name-entry.mjs — and used them alongside the item's named tools rather than instead of them.
method_deviations.why: Rule 24 / TOOL-LOOP: RI-JRN01 O6, O7, O17 and RI-CHR01 §1 all describe a player doing things, and every probe in the tree drives the scene through __HARNESS mutators. No tool existed that boots the game the way a human's browser boots it and dispatches real DOM input. The two blocking defects in this verdict are both invisible to every harness-driven probe and were found in the first ten minutes of running one that is not.

method_deviations.why: main.js selects harness mode from navigator.webdriver, which Playwright sets. Forcing it false removes the automation tell and leaves the game untouched; passing ?mode=play would be a flag, and NEXT-DISPATCH §P gate item 1 says 'no flags'.

method_deviations.deviation: Scored unmeasurable => 0 without running a 60-minute driven session, and hard fails 2, 3 and 4 not fired despite being literally satisfied.

Firing 2/3/4 on an undriven hour makes the whole wave DEAD under PLAYTHROUGH-CRITIC §2 on an artifact of who ran the session — which is measuring the toolchain, the error BAR-CRITIQUE-W1-07-R1 §R1 was written to end.

method_deviations.deviation: HF1 read per node (hold.out = 0.000) as well as per node kind (the two paused/auto nodes aggregate to 0 drawn of 2 computed).
method_deviations.why: Round 1 established the per-node reading in this piece's own history with the argument that a threshold cannot be read one way to clear it and another way to clear it again. I checked HF1 fires under both readings before applying the one that costs the build.

arbitration_questions: RI-JRN09 M1's hard fail is 'DTR < 0.50 on any node class' and the item defines DTR at three granularities without defining 'node class'. Round 1 filed this and it is still open. It now decides a second verdict: hold.out is 0.000 per node AND 0.000 as a class, so it does not change this outcome, but the next build that lands a 0.4 on one node and 0.6 on its class will turn on it.

RI-JRN01 M13/HF5 says the journey must be completable on four modalities. When the journey is incompletable for a reason that has nothing to do with input modality, does HF5 fire? I ruled that it does, on M13's literal text ('any run that cannot complete'), and I note that the same root cause then caps two items. A ruling that HF5 is modality-specific would move RI-JRN01 from 2 to its band ceiling of 6 and would not change the piece's status.
